## The claim

P4-22: approved statins selectively inhibit rhabdomyosarcoma cell lines in the PRISM repurposing screen

**Prediction if true.** RMS lines are more sensitive than non-RMS lines to at least one approved statin (one-sided rank test p < 0.05, lineage-aware), with most statins in the same direction

**What would refute it.** no approved statin shows RMS selectivity at p < 0.2, or most statins point the other way

## Evidence

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 202 | supports | 0.40 | measurement | In PRISM Repurposing 24Q2 (6,790 compounds × 919 lines), 4 of the 5 approved statins measurable on ≥ 3 of the 14 rhabdomyosarcoma lines are more sensitive in those lines; simvastatin Cliff's δ +0.681 (95 % CI 0.417–0.875, n 3 vs 528, one-sided p 0.0189) and rosuvastatin δ +0.274 (−0.070–0.557, n 14 vs 858, p 0.0394). | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/151-prism-replication-of-the-track2-leads.md` |
| 203 | neutral | 0.30 | measurement | No statin survives Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 24 candidates (best q = 0.132), and the negative-control band for the same contrast spans Cliff's δ −0.73 to +0.67, so a 3-line result of δ +0.68 is inside the noise. | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/151-prism-replication-of-the-track2-leads.md` |
| 204 | neutral | 0.30 | measurement | Against other soft-tissue lines only, rosuvastatin reaches δ +0.584 (0.169–0.922, n 14 vs 11, p 0.0074); lovastatin, pravastatin and mevastatin are measured on 2 rhabdomyosarcoma lines and cannot be tested. | `docs/iteration4/step-9/methodology/151-prism-replication-of-the-track2-leads.md` |
